book_paragraphs: Welcome to the Research Desk underwriting monograph for KORU—the Direxion Daily MSCI South Korea Bull 3X ETF, officially renamed from Shares in March 2026. Before we examine ten chapters of SEC filings, swap books, and market action, let us state our findings and portfolio action plainly.

In Pass 1, completely blind to the live share price, we audited KORU's FY2025 Form N-CSR alongside its 1H FY2026 Form N-CSRS, July 2026 Form NPORT-P, and August 2026 EWY holdings. KORU runs clean institutional plumbing across $747.35 million in November 2026 assets, 33.52 million shares in daily volume, and seven Tier-1 swap dealers—earning CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality and PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. Yet 2026 filings exposed serious hidden frictions: Citibank doubled its swap spread to SOFR plus 1.70%, six-month turnover spiked to 264%, MMF collateral yields slipped to 3.52%–3.55% below 3.91% SOFR, and Samsung plus SK chaebol look-through concentration exceeded 56%.

In Pass 2, unlocking the November 20, 2026 market tape removed every shred of ambiguity. KORU plunged -25.04% on Friday to close at $4.76—down 92.56% from its $63.99 high, down 80.64% below its $24.59 30-week SMA, and sitting just 3.7% above its $4.59 52-week low. While unleveraged EWY gained +33.40% over the past year, KORU lost -37.16% due to negative carry (-8.43% to -8.65% annually) and severe discrete variance drag at 60%–65% index volatility. Both KORU and EWY sit in confirmed Stage 4 while the S&P 500 trades in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend.

Accordingly, our New-Capital Verdict is REJECTED (TREND, VALUATION, CASH_FLOW) at TIER_0, with our probability-weighted 12-month expected price at $3.08 (Base $2.70, Bear $1.28, Bull $7.07) and options rated NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. For your 471.984153 shares in Robinhood ($2,246.64 market value vs $5,457.78 cost, -$3,211.14 / -58.84% loss, 2.99% weight, 8.35 beta), the $4.76 close breached the prior $5.22 stop—mandating EXIT_IMMEDIATELY and deploying 100% ($2,246.64) into CASH.

book_subsections.title: 0.1 What KORU Is and Why It Failed Every Pass 2 Gate
paragraphs: KORU is a single-day 300% leveraged ETF managed by Rafferty Asset Management under the Direxion Shares ETF Trust. It combines physical EWY shares (51.3% in April 2026) and money market collateral (44.1% yielding 3.52%–3.55%) with over-the-counter total return swaps across seven global banks. Because Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and affiliated chaebol entities exceed 56% of the underlying index, KORU acts as a Won-sensitive Korean semiconductor amplifier.

On November 20, 2026, KORU closed at $4.76 (-37.16% 1Y vs EWY +33.40% 1Y) in confirmed Stage 4, bleeding roughly -8.43% to -8.65% annually in negative carry plus -66% to -71% discrete variance drag at 60%–65% index volatility. With probability-weighted 12-month value at $3.08 ($2.70 Base Case), KORU fails Trend, Valuation math, and Cash-Flow carry gates.
